sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Aalen sets on-street fees by ordinance, while the central garages are run by the municipal Stadtwerke. The Gemeinderat adopted the current Parkgebührensatzung on 18 May 2017, in force from 1 September 2017, with 50 cents per 20 minutes at meters, a maximum stay of 120 minutes, and a €6 day ticket at the Ostalbklinikum machines [4]. In February 2022 the mayor, Frederick Brütting, applied the same ordinance to the Kulturbahnhof car park, which had been outside the city's parking-management concept; he described it as a fee reduction for guests [11]. Free parking has been asked for and refused: in the December 2023 budget debate the council rejected an AfD request to extend free parking in the Stadtwerke garages from 20 minutes to one hour [14]. In June 2021 the administration had proposed a free first hour for July to September of that year, at about €15,000 a month, but the article does not give the outcome of the vote [10]. In August 2024 Brütting called an FDP programme that included dropping parking charges a regression to the 1970s, while a retail representative said free parking was not the answer [15].

Two measures are still at an early stage. In December 2024 the council passed, unanimously, a basic resolution (Grundsatzbeschluss) to pursue extending the pedestrian zone, and the mayor said one to two years were needed to clear open questions; he also spoke of a possible parking garage on the east side of the centre [19]. In January 2026 the council voted to explore camera scan vehicles for enforcement, a Green proposal that the administration will test against pilots in Mannheim and Heidelberg before any final decision [24].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The development is mostly in how the garages are run, not in new ones. In December 2015 it was reported that the Rathaus underground garage, then 255 spaces, would close from 11 January 2016 for a refurbishment costing about €4 million, and the Parkplatz Kubus with 35 spaces above its entrance opened on 6 October 2017 [3][5]. The Spritzenhausplatz garage was renovated over about a year, with a February 2018 promotion to raise awareness of it [7]. In 2020 the state interior ministry announced €334,015 of funding for a planned dynamic parking guidance system [8]. An August 2024 press report said an intelligent parking guidance system recording 2,000 spaces had gone into operation [15]. In autumn 2024 Stadtwerke Aalen was converting its garages to licence-plate recognition, with the Rathaus garage still scheduled for early November and the rest done or set for November [16].

Commuters are the other focus. From 1 January 2025 the station garage (P6) offers commuter passes at €45.50 a month, €136.50 for six months and €253.50 a year with proof of rail commuter status, and lower caps for occasional parkers [20]. A start-up, PEUKA, began renting 20 private spaces by the hour in January 2025; the city manager doubted the model would work in a city this size because the municipal garages have ample evening capacity [21]. We found no sourced figures on garage capacity changes or on parking at the shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Aalen data cover five Stadtwerke garages with 1,292 spaces: the station garage P6 (390), Reichsstädter Markt P2 (310), Rathaus P1 (251), Spitalstraße P5 (190) and Spritzenhausplatz P3 (151). The sources describe these as the municipal facilities; the Mercatura shopping-centre garage is run separately by B+B Parkhaus and is not in our data [12]. Capacities differ from the sources in places: a 2015 article gives 409 spaces for Reichsstädter Markt against 310 in the feed, and 255 for the Rathaus garage against 251 [3].

Occupancy from August to early October 2026 averaged about 61% on weekdays and 58% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The station garage is the fullest at 71%, then Reichsstädter Markt at 66%, Spritzenhausplatz at 62%, Rathaus at 54% and Spitalstraße at 43%. P2 and P6 stay as busy at weekends as on weekdays (66% and 70%), while P5 falls from 43% to 36%. Every garage peaks at 10 or 11 in the morning; averaged over the weeks, the busiest hour reaches 97% at the Rathaus, 96% at Spitalstraße and 94% at Spritzenhausplatz, but only about 80% at P2 and P6. The window includes the summer holidays.

The Stadtwerke tariff has changed in each of the last three years. From 1 January 2024 the first 20 minutes stayed free, the first hour cost €1 and the daily maximum was €12 [12]. From 1 January 2026 Stadtwerke Aalen announced €0.50 for up to 30 minutes, free for energy customers with the customer card, €1.50 for each further hour after the first, a daily maximum of €12.50 and a €4 night maximum from midnight to 6 a.m. [22]. Short-term parking at the five facilities rose from 805,539 vehicles in 2024 to 1,031,224 in 2025, about 28% more; the article does not explain the jump [25]. The Stadtwerke expected about €195,000 of extra revenue from the 2026 changes and still forecast a low six-figure deficit for the year [25].
